precision: rates are statutory and stable; the socialSecurityWageBase is UNVERIFIED for 2026 and is the single figure to check before relying on any output above it
source: Self-employment tax mechanics: IRC 1401/1402. The 92.35% adjustment, the 15.3% combined rate and the deductible employer-equivalent half are long-standing statute. The wage base is indexed annually and must be re-checked.
confidenceNote: Mechanics are IRC 1401/1402 and long-standing statute. The wage base is indexed annually and is the one figure to re-check.
note: SPEC.md Section 13 flags SE tax as a common source of off-by-a-factor errors, so every step is named here rather than folded into one multiplication: net earnings are 92.35% of net profit; Social Security applies to those earnings up to the wage base; Medicare applies with no cap; an additional Medicare levy applies above a filing-status threshold; and half the combined Social Security and Medicare tax is deductible against income tax.

additionalMedicare.note: Not deductible, and applies to the earnings above the threshold only.

employeeFicaNote: What a W2 employee pays. The employer pays the matching half, which is the core of the W2-vs-1099 comparison.

safeHarbor.note: Estimated payments avoid an underpayment penalty if they cover the lesser of 90% of this year's liability or 100% of last year's — 110% when last year's AGI exceeded the high-income threshold.
